title: Her 101-year-old grandmother and a few Senegalese words
summary: Alice remembers her grandmother, who died in 1910 aged 101, and the African words she taught her, such as 'Salicum Serum' for good morning.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Can you remember your parents and your grandmother too? You told me about your grandmother once.
If I remember my grandmother, oh Lord, yes. If I remember my grandmother. Seems like she's right in front of me now. And I miss her. I miss her. She was 101 years and 15 days when she died.
101. Well, you may make that too.
No, no, I don't hope that.
Well, if you're well, unless you're well, there's no need to live. Yes, if I was well. But you look well.
She died on the 15th day of January. And she was 101 year on the 1st of January. She died 101 year and 15 days.
1910, yes. You remember her then real well. Yes, I remember her well.
You told me once that she taught you some Senegalese, the African language, a few words.

Because I used to be right by her all the time. I idolized my grandmother. And she spoke her mother's language. But my mother and my aunt and them, they didn't want her yet that. But me, I would be right there by her. And I tell her, Gagan, because I didn't call her grandma, I called her Gagan. I say, Gagan, tell me, tell me. And she would tell me. And sometimes she'd say, Abadra. Abadra, that means good for nothing. That's Senegal.
What was good morning? You told me that, I think, once.
Salicum Serum. Salicum Serum is good morning, everybody.
